papers.title: SIK3 isoforms and PKA phosphorylation sites differentially regulate sleep and circadian rhythms.
papers.summary: The study generated isoform-selective SIK3 knock-in mice and PKA-phosphorylation site mutants to dissect isoform-specific functions in sleep and circadian regulation. They found that the 150 kDa SIK3 isoform controls wakefulness at dark onset and circadian period, while the 70 kDa isoform affects NREM sleep delta power, and alanine substitution at T469 or S551 produced hypersomnia.

papers.title: Circadian Rhythms in a Petri Dish: Synchronizing Mouse Hypothalamic mHypoE-42 Cells for Circadian Clock Gene Expression Analysis.
papers.summary: This methods paper presents a detailed protocol for synchronizing cultured mHypoE-42 hypothalamic cells using serum shock, followed by time-course sampling and analysis of circadian clock gene expression via qRT-PCR with appropriate statistical methods. The protocol aims to standardize in vitro circadian experiments for reproducibility.

papers.title: The Expression and Effects of Rev-Erbα in Different Cerebral Regions of Mice With Acute and Chronic Epilepsy.
papers.summary: This study examined Rev-Erbα expression in the medial prefrontal cortex, hippocampus, and occipital visual cortex of mice with acute and chronic epilepsy, and tested the effects of the Rev-Erbα agonist SR9009. They found that SR9009 reduced seizure activity, abnormal EEG discharges, and improved anxiety-like behavior and spatial memory, suggesting antiepileptic and neuroprotective roles.

papers.title: Sleep spindle state-dependent motor cortical plasticity induction by EEG-triggered ripple burst TMS
papers.summary: The study tested EEG-triggered TMS targeting different sleep spindle states in sleeping participants and found that only spindle-trough stimulation induced robust long-term depression-like motor cortical plasticity, with no consistent changes from other phases.

papers.title: Sensory-sleep dysfunction is a shared phenotype across genetically distinct neurodevelopmental disorder models
papers.summary: This study examined vibration-induced sleep (VIS) in three Drosophila models of neurodevelopmental disorders (dNf1, dNrx1, dFmr1) and found that all three exhibited impaired VIS despite different baseline sleep phenotypes, identifying disrupted sensory-sleep integration as a shared phenotype. The effect of mechanosensory stimulation was modulated by homeostatic sleep drive, and distinct abnormalities were found in behavioral responses, CRTC signaling, and neuron activation across models.

papers.title: From co-occurrence to increasingly precise temporal coordination: Development of slow oscillation-spindle coupling from infancy to toddlerhood
papers.summary: This study investigated the development of slow oscillation (SO)-spindle coupling from infancy to toddlerhood using EEG recordings in 9- to 16-month-olds. Results show that SO-spindle co-occurrence exceeds chance levels in infants at central regions and becomes more precise with age, suggesting the coupling emerges in the second half of the first year and strengthens into toddlerhood.

papers.title: Boundary-Dependent Sleep-Wake Dysregulation in Idiopathic Hypersomnia.
papers.journal: Annals of clinical and translational neurology
papers.summary: In idiopathic hypersomnia (IH), patients show excessive stabilization of NREM sleep with fewer transitions to wakefulness and reduced spindle amplitude, suggesting altered sleep-wake dynamics rather than sleep loss contribute to daytime sleepiness.

papers.title: Age-Dependent Effects of Caffeine on Physiological, Behavioral, and Circadian Gene Changes in Young and Mature C57BL/6 Male Mice.
papers.summary: This study investigated age-dependent effects of caffeine on body weight, behavior, and circadian gene expression in young and mature male mice. Caffeine improved balance and coordination, altered circadian gene expression (Clock, Bmal1, Per2, Cry1, Cry2) in brain and Neuro 2a cells, and modulated adenosine receptor levels with age differences.

papers.title: Circadian alignment as a dimension of adolescent sleep health and self-regulation.
papers.summary: The abstract is missing, so no findings can be summarized. The title suggests a study on the relationship between circadian alignment, sleep health, and self-regulation in adolescents.

papers.title: Phasic activities in the human body during REM sleep Part 2: Autonomic activity and general discussion.
papers.summary: This review catalogs phasic autonomic activities during human REM sleep, including pupillary, cardiovascular, respiratory, and reproductive changes, and discusses how they cluster with rapid eye movements and muscle twitches.

papers.title: EEG spectral analysis of nighttime sleep and daytime MSLTs and neurocognitive evaluations in obstructive sleep apnea patients with residual sleepiness.
papers.summary: This case-control study of obstructive sleep apnea patients with residual excessive sleepiness (RES) used EEG spectral analysis and cognitive assessments, finding that RES patients exhibit increased delta/theta power and decreased alpha/beta power during sleep and wakefulness, alongside multidimensional cognitive impairments including executive function, processing speed, working memory, and attention. These EEG patterns were associated with distinct cognitive deficits.

papers.title: From screens to live interactions: Considerations for naturalistic EEG paradigms in social and affective neuroscience.
papers.summary: This paper reviews analytic decisions in live, interactive EEG paradigms and evaluates their effects using infant EEG data from a mother-infant task. It identifies varying analytic approaches (e.g., analysis window, inclusion of usable EEG, covariates) that can change results, and recommends best practices for reporting and decision-making to improve transparency and replicability.

papers.title: Astrocyte molecular rhythm disruption in nucleus accumbens promotes increased binge-like drinking in mice
papers.summary: This study investigated the role of astrocyte molecular rhythms in alcohol drinking by disrupting clock function in nucleus accumbens (NAc) astrocytes of mice. Results showed that astrocytic BMAL1 knockout increased binge-like drinking in drinking-in-the-light and drinking-in-the-dark paradigms but not in other drinking behaviors, suggesting a unique role for astrocyte rhythms in temporal regulation of reward and binge drinking.

papers.title: Napping improves interhemispheric functional coordination during night shifts in nurses: analysis of voxel-mirrored homotopic connectivity.
papers.summary: In a crossover study of 21 female nurses, night shift napping reduced the sleep deprivation-induced increase in interhemispheric functional connectivity (VMHC) and improved neurocognitive performance.

papers.title: Skipjack tuna peptides exert sleep-promoting effects by regulating neurotransmitter metabolism in pentobarbital sodium-induced mice.
papers.summary: Skipjack tuna peptide GHHAA (S4) dose-dependently promoted sleep in pentobarbital sodium-induced mice by increasing inhibitory neurotransmitters (GABA) and c-Fos expression in the VLPO, while decreasing excitatory neurotransmitters.

papers.title: Nocturnal peak in cardiac baroreflex effectiveness aligns with nocturnal trough in systolic blood pressure in young healthy adults: Possible circadian effects.
papers.summary: In 11 healthy adults, a 30-h circadian protocol showed that the nocturnal peak in cardiac baroreflex effectiveness index (BEI) at ~1 am aligned with the systolic blood pressure trough at ~1:40 am, while baroreflex sensitivity showed no circadian variation. This alignment suggests a possible circadian influence on baroreflex function.

papers.title: Magnetoencephalography Source Analysis in Epilepsy-Aphasia Spectrum.
papers.summary: MEG source analysis of 70 epilepsy-aphasia spectrum patients revealed distinct source distributions and current densities across subtypes, with a gradient from temporo-centric (SeLECTS, LKS) to fronto-centric (EE-SWAS, ABPE), paralleling clinical severity.

papers.title: Unveiling the inflammatory link: integrated analysis identifies BMP7 and PPBP as key genes in obstructive sleep apnea-related atrial fibrillation.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: Using integrated bioinformatics on OSA and AF datasets plus clinical and rat model validation, this study identified BMP7 downregulation and PPBP upregulation as key genes linking obstructive sleep apnea to atrial fibrillation, with a nomogram showing good diagnostic performance (AUC=0.843).

papers.title: Polysomnographic Parameters in Schizoaffective Disorder: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis compared polysomnographic sleep measures in drug-free schizoaffective disorder (SZA) patients versus healthy controls and related psychiatric groups. SZA patients showed reduced total sleep time, increased sleep latency and wake after sleep onset, and REM abnormalities, but no reliable differences from schizophrenia or major depressive disorder.

papers.title: Pediatric Sleep Assessment through Spectral Sleep Scoring: A Comparison with Polysomnography
papers.summary: This study validated a spectral scoring method for pediatric sleep against visual polysomnography scoring, achieving high agreement (kappa=0.76) across sleep stages. The method may offer efficient, developmentally sensitive sleep assessment for pediatric populations.

papers.title: Non-Covalent Poly(ADP-ribose) Signaling Organizes a Circadian E3 Ligase Network in the Brain
papers.summary: This study integrated brain transcriptomics, genetic associations, circadian phase annotations, and single-cell data to characterize PAR-binding E3 ubiquitin ligases in the brain, finding that they form a regionally structured, circadian-organized network with distinct phase relationships to clock genes and microglial enrichment. The analysis suggests non-covalent PAR signaling coordinates time-dependent ubiquitin control in neural systems.

papers.title: Characterization of the circadian system in binge eating disorder and the effects of morning bright light and individually timed exogenous melatonin administration: A 4-week feasibility double-blind randomized controlled mechanistic clinical trial.
papers.summary: This two-phase study compared circadian phase (DLMO) between adults with binge eating disorder (BED) and controls, finding no group difference but a correlation between later DLMO and greater BED severity, plus reduced actigraphy amplitude in BED. In a 4-week RCT, morning bright light plus individually timed melatonin did not significantly change DLMO vs sham, but later baseline DLMO correlated with greater phase advance and binge reduction.

papers.title: Adolescent circadian sleep health: a review of multimodal assessment strategies and clinical implications.
papers.summary: This review defines key circadian sleep health concepts (chronotype, circadian timing, circadian alignment) and synthesizes best practices for multimodal assessment in adolescents, covering self-report, behavioral, and physiological tools, along with contextual factors. It emphasizes the value of combining subjective and objective measures to improve clinical utility and future research directions.

papers.title: Circadian regulators PER1 and PER2 control osteoclastogenesis in male mice through coordinated regulation of opposing innate immunity genes.
papers.journal: Journal of bone and mineral research : the official journal of the American Society for Bone and Mineral Research
papers.summary: This study examined osteoclast-specific deletion of both Per1 and Per2 in mice and found suppression of osteoclastogenesis and increased bone mass in males, opposite to Per1 single knockout. Transcriptomic and ChIP analyses indicate PER1 and PER2 regulate osteoclastogenesis through coordinated control of innate immunity genes with opposing effects.

papers.title: Modafinil ameliorates sleep deprivation-induced memory impairment under acute hypobaric hypoxia via biphasic Cyp3a11 regulation and altered pharmacokinetics.
papers.journal: The Journal of pharmacology and experimental therapeutics
papers.summary: In a mouse model combining acute hypobaric hypoxia and sleep deprivation, modafinil improved cognitive deficits but its pharmacokinetics were altered, with delayed elimination associated with biphasic Cyp3a11 regulation and progressive liver injury.

papers.title: Wearable Sleep and Circadian Monitoring in Intensive Care Nursing: A Scoping Review.
papers.summary: This scoping review of 61 reports on wearable sleep and circadian monitoring in intensive care found that actigraphy dominates, but measurement performance varies by device, patient state, and age, particularly with poor wake specificity in ventilated or sedated patients. Wearables are useful for describing rest-activity patterns but are not a standalone sleep measure.

papers.title: Sleepiness During Night Shifts and Nurses' Self-Reported Cognitive Control, Cognitive Flexibility, and Handover Effectiveness: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 270 nurses, higher sleepiness during night shifts was associated with lower self-reported cognitive control, cognitive flexibility, and handover effectiveness, with cognitive control mediating the sleepiness-handover link. The findings highlight sleepiness as an occupational risk warranting monitoring and organizational strategies.

papers.title: Antipsychotics and Sleep Architecture: Where Does Lurasidone Fit?
papers.summary: This narrative review summarizes the neurobiology of sleep and receptor-based hypotheses of how lurasidone, an antipsychotic with low sedation liability, may affect sleep architecture, concluding that direct human evidence for sleep architecture modification is limited and that lurasidone's sleep-related benefits beyond psychiatric symptom improvement remain unproven. Most important contribution is the synthesis of available evidence and identification of gaps, including need for long-term polysomnography and circadian biomarker studies.

papers.title: Lactobacillus acidophilus CICC 22162 alleviates sleep deprivation-induced cognitive impairment by remodeling gut microbiota and enhancing S-adenosylmethionine-mediated neuroimmune regulation.
papers.summary: This study in a mouse model found that Lactobacillus acidophilus CICC 22162 alleviates sleep deprivation-induced cognitive impairment by remodeling gut microbiota and enhancing S-adenosylmethionine-mediated neuroimmune regulation, involving α7nAChR signaling.

papers.title: Comparative Evaluation of Changes in Brain Activity Among Edentulous Patients Rehabilitated With Conventional Complete Dentures and Tooth-Supported Overdentures Using Electroencephalography: An In Vivo Study.
papers.summary: This prospective observational study in edentulous patients found that prosthodontic rehabilitation with conventional complete dentures or tooth-supported overdentures significantly increased EEG-derived cortical brain activity after two months, with no significant differences between prosthesis types.

papers.title: Chrononutrition and Pediatric Metabolic Health: An Integrative Review of Circadian Biology and Early-Day Metabolic Regulation.
papers.summary: This integrative review synthesizes evidence from chronobiology and pediatric nutrition to propose the Early-Day Metabolic Window (EMW) and the Costa Reset Conceptual Model, suggesting that early-day eating patterns influence pediatric metabolic regulation through circadian synchronization and endocrine responsiveness. The framework is conceptual and requires experimental validation.

papers.title: The relationship of peripheral circadian gene mRNAs, antisense lncRNAs, and serum protein levels with chronotype, biological, and social rhythm in euthymic patients with bipolar disorder.
papers.summary: In 60 euthymic bipolar disorder patients, peripheral mRNA levels of CIART and CLOCK and antisense lncRNAs PER2AS and CRY1AS were higher than in controls, with differences concentrated in BD-2 and ASHH subtypes. Serum protein levels and behavioral rhythm scores did not differ, underscoring a divergence across measurement levels.

papers.title: Dorsolateral nigral hyperintensity in idiopathic REM sleep behavior disorder: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis found that visual assessment of dorsolateral nigral hyperintensity on MRI has high specificity but moderate sensitivity for differentiating idiopathic REM sleep behavior disorder from healthy controls, and it correlates with abnormal dopamine transporter imaging.

papers.title: Perioperative immunocircadian recovery and its association with circulating tumor DNA-based minimal residual disease and long-term survival after colorectal cancer surgery.
papers.summary: In a prospective cohort of 1,000 colorectal cancer patients, delayed perioperative immunocircadian recovery was associated with higher circulating tumor DNA-based minimal residual disease positivity and worse disease-free and overall survival, adding prognostic value beyond conventional factors.

papers.title: Shielding the First 24 Postnatal Months of Life: A Proposal for a Prospective Cohort Study of Early-Life Electromagnetic Exposure and Autism Risk.
papers.summary: This paper proposes a prospective cohort study protocol to test whether reducing electromagnetic radiation (EMR) exposure during the first 24 months of life can modulate autism spectrum disorder (ASD) risk. The protocol outlines a two-arm design (EMR-reduced with Faraday shielding vs. standard exposure) measuring neurodevelopmental outcomes and exploratory ASD diagnoses, powered for signal detection rather than definitive inference.

papers.title: Bidirectional links between food intake and sleep: a naturalistic mobile EEG study
papers.summary: This naturalistic study used mobile EEG and questionnaires in healthy participants to examine bidirectional time-lagged within-person associations between sleep and food intake, finding that later last meal timing predicted later sleep onset, longer fasting to sleep predicted reduced total sleep time and efficiency, and later sleep shifted next-day eating later. It concluded that links are primarily timing-related, with no negative effect of large, late, or satiating meals on sleep quality.

papers.title: Oocyte quality in endometriosis-associated infertility: a narrative analysis of mechanisms and therapeutic options.
papers.summary: This narrative review summarizes mechanisms by which endometriosis impairs oocyte quality, including inflammation, oxidative stress, and mitochondrial dysfunction, and discusses therapeutic options such as lifestyle modifications and ART.

papers.title: Electroencephalography Functional Network Responses to Immersive Virtual Reality in Alzheimer Disease and Mild Cognitive Impairment: Exploratory Single-Session 3-Group Repeated-Measures Study.
papers.summary: This exploratory single-session repeated-measures EEG study in 60 older adults (AD, MCI, NC) found that immersive VR exposure altered EEG functional network organization state-dependently, with higher global efficiency in AD than NC at baseline but no significant group differences during VR, and within-group increases in efficiency from pre-VR to VR in NC and pre-VR to post-VR in MCI. The study demonstrates feasibility of VR-EEG for characterizing network responsiveness but provides no confirmatory evidence of causality or therapeutic efficacy.

papers.title: EEG Analysis of Visual Attention Under Perception of Affective Prosody in Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder.
papers.summary: This study analyzed EEG theta-beta ratio (TBR) in children with ASD and TD during multiple object tracking tasks under happy/sad prosody, finding higher TBR in ASD across all brain regions and an interaction between attention level and emotion for global and temporal TBR, with temporal TBR differing between emotions during high-load tracking. It provides evidence for altered attention-emotion interaction in ASD, particularly in temporal regions.

papers.title: Case Report: SMART syndrome mimicking Todd's paralysis after meningioma irradiation.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 59-year-old male with SMART syndrome mimicking Todd's paralysis after irradiation for meningioma, presenting with seizures and progressive neurologic deficits. The patient improved with dexamethasone and amlodipine, highlighting SMART syndrome as a diagnosis of exclusion with a shortened latency and rare association with meningioma.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
